parts.text: In this experiment, you will investigate the resistance of a wire. Carry out the following instructions referring to Fig. 3.1, which shows the circuit that has been set up for you. Fig. 3.1 You are provided with a length of resistance wire AB .

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Place the sliding contact C on the resistance wire AB at a distance x from A , where x = 0.100 m.

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) Record the value of x in Table 3.1.

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) Switch on. Using the voltmeter, measure the p.d. V across the wire between A and C . Record the value of V in Table 3.1.

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) Using the ammeter, measure the current I in the wire. Record the value of I . I = .......................................................... [1]

parts.label: e
parts.text: (e) Take the sliding contact away from the wire AB and switch off.

parts.label: f
parts.text: (f) Calculate the resistance R of the section AC of the wire using the equation R = V I .

parts.label: g
parts.text: (g) Record R in the table. Table 3.1 x / m V / V R / Ω [3]

parts.label: h
parts.text: (h) Repeat steps (a) to (g) with the sliding contact at distances of x = 0.300 m, 0.500 m, 0.700 m and 0.900 m from A .

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Plot a graph of R / Ω ( y -axis) against x / m ( x -axis). [3]

parts.label: k
parts.text: (k) Using your graph, determine a value for the resistance R when the length x = 0.750 m. Show clearly on your graph how you obtained the necessary information. R = .......................................................... [2]
